facts.text: The Constitution is the fundamental and the highest law of the land.
facts.quote: Our Constitution is the fundamental and the highest law of the land.

facts.text: A systematic arrangement of all the aims and objectives of a law is the Preface to the law.
facts.quote: A systematic arrangement of all the aims and objectives of a law is the Preface to the law.

facts.text: The Preface to the Indian Constitution is called the Preamble; it sets out the objectives of the Constitution.
facts.quote: The Preface to the Indian Constitution is called the 'Preamble'. The Preamble sets out the objectives of our Constitution.

facts.text: The Preamble begins with the words 'We, the people of India'.
facts.quote: The Preamble begins with the words, 'We, the people of India'.

facts.text: The Preamble talks of the resolve to constitute India into a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic.
facts.quote: It talks about the resolve of the Indians to constitute India into a 'Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic'.

facts.text: British rule ended on 15th August 1947; India became independent and sovereign.
facts.quote: The British rule ended on 15th August 1947. Our country became independent. India became sovereign.

facts.text: Sovereign means that a State is not under the control of a foreign power.
facts.quote: The word sovereign means that a State is not under the control of a foreign power.

facts.text: The most important goal of the freedom struggle was to acquire sovereignty.
facts.quote: The most important goal of our freedom struggle was to acquire sovereignty.

facts.text: Sovereignty means the ultimate authority to govern yourself; in a democracy it rests with the people.
facts.quote: Sovereignty means the ultimate authority to govern yourself. In a democracy, sovereignty rests with the people.

facts.text: The Constitution reflects the principle of popular sovereignty; the government elected by the people makes laws on their behalf.
facts.quote: Thus the Constitution reflects the principle of popular sovereignty and the government elected by the people makes laws on behalf of the people.

facts.text: In a Socialist State the gap between the rich and the poor is minimum and wealth is not concentrated in a few hands.
facts.quote: A Socialist State is such a State where the gap between the rich and the poor is minimum. ... It is ensured that wealth is not concentrated in the hands of a few people.

facts.text: In a Secular State all religions are considered equal and no one religion is the State religion.
facts.quote: In a secular State, all religions are considered as equal. No one religion is considered to be the State religion.

facts.text: In a Secular State citizens are free to follow their own religion and the State cannot discriminate on the basis of religion.
facts.quote: The citizens are free to follow their own religion. State cannot discriminate among citizens on the basis of religion.

facts.text: We have endeavoured to preserve the multi-religious nature of our society; while celebrating festivals we must care about public cleanliness, health and the environment.
facts.quote: We have endeavoured to preserve the multi-religious nature of our society. ... Whenever we celebrate our festivals, we are required to be concerned about public cleanliness, health and the environment.

facts.text: In a democracy the sovereign power is in the hands of the people; elections are held after a fixed period because all the people cannot decide day to day.
facts.quote: In a democracy, the sovereign power is in the hands of the people. ... All the people are not able to come together and take such decisions on a day-to-day basis. Therefore, elections are conducted after a fixed period

facts.text: Elected representatives sit in institutions like the Parliament or Legislature and the Executive.
facts.quote: These representatives sit in the institutions created by the Constitution like the Parliament or Legislature and the Executive.

facts.text: In a Republic all public positions are elected by the people; none is occupied by hereditary succession.
facts.quote: All public positions in a Republic are elected by the people. No public position is occupied on the basis of hereditary succession.

facts.text: President, Prime Minister, Governor, Chief Minister, Mayor and Sarpanch are public positions open to any citizen meeting the age criterion.
facts.quote: The positions like the President, the Prime Minister, the Governor, the Chief Minister, the Mayor, the Sarpanch, etc. are public positions. Any Indian citizen fulfilling the prescribed age criterion can get himself/herself elected

facts.text: In a monarchy, public positions may be occupied by members of a single family following the principle of heredity.
facts.quote: In a monarchy, these positions may be occupied by members of a single family following the principle of heredity.

facts.text: Deepa wrote on 'My Family'; even the grandparents are consulted and Anuja wants to take up agricultural research.
facts.quote: Read what Deepa has written on the topic : 'My Family'. ... even the grandparents are consulted. Anuja wants to take up agricultural research as her career.

facts.text: The Preamble guarantees the three values of Justice, Liberty and Equality.
facts.quote: The Preamble has guaranteed the Indian citizens the three values of Justice, Liberty and Equality.

facts.text: Justice implies removal of injustice and ensuring that everybody has the opportunity for progress; it means policies that promote public good.
facts.quote: Justice implies removal of injustice and ensuring that everybody has the opportunity for progress. Establishing justice is adopting such policies that will promote public good.

facts.text: Three types of justice are talked of in the Preamble: social, economic and political.
facts.quote: Three types of justice are talked of in the Preamble. ... (a) Social Justice ... (b) Economic Justice ... (c) Political Justice

facts.text: Social justice: no discrimination on the basis of caste, creed, race, language, region, place of birth or sex.
facts.quote: There should be no discrimination among individuals on the basis of caste, creed, race, language, region, place of birth or sex.

facts.text: Economic justice: poverty leads to hunger, hunger-deaths or malnourishment, so everyone should have the right to a source of livelihood.
facts.quote: Poverty leads to the evils of hunger, hunger-deaths or malnourishment. If poverty is to be eradicated, everyone should have the right to a source of livelihood

facts.text: Political justice: universal adult franchise; all citizens completing 18 years of age have the right to vote.
facts.quote: We have adopted universal adult franchise to enable equal participation in the running of the country. Accordingly, all citizens completing 18 years of age have the right to vote in elections.

facts.text: Liberty means no coercive, unfair restrictions; democracy becomes mature only if citizens enjoy freedom.
facts.quote: Liberty implies that there should be no coercive, unfair restrictions upon us ... democracy becomes mature only if citizens enjoy freedom.

facts.text: Freedom of thought and expression is the most fundamental freedom for an individual.
facts.quote: Freedom of thought and expression is the most fundamental freedom for an individual.

facts.text: The liberty of belief, faith and worship implies religious freedom.
facts.quote: The liberty of belief, faith and worship implies religious freedom.

facts.text: The Preamble guarantees an equality of status and of opportunity.
facts.quote: The Preamble guarantees the Indian citizens an equality of status and of opportunity.

facts.text: Equal status means not to discriminate between people in terms of high-low, superior-inferior.
facts.quote: The guarantee of equal status means not to discriminate between people in terms of high-low, superior-inferior.

facts.text: The Preamble's unique ideal is promoting fraternity and assuring the dignity of the individual.
facts.quote: It is the goal of promoting fraternity among the citizens and to assure the dignity of the individual.

facts.text: Fraternity implies a 'we-feeling' towards one another and creates a feeling of empathy.
facts.quote: Fraternity implies a 'we-feeling' towards one another. It creates a feeling of empathy.

facts.text: The makers of the Constitution believed no amount of laws would achieve the goals if fraternity is lacking, so fraternity was included as a goal.
facts.quote: No amount of laws would help us achieve these goals if fraternity is lacking among Indians. Hence the promotion of fraternity has been included in the Preamble as a goal.

facts.text: Fraternity is closely related to human dignity; human dignity implies equal respect to each individual as a human being, not depending on caste, creed, race, sex or language.
facts.quote: Fraternity is closely related to human dignity. Human dignity implies equal respect to each individual as a human being. It does not depend upon the criteria of caste, creed, race, sex, language, etc.

facts.text: When every individual respects another and honours their freedom and rights, dignity gets established and fraternity grows automatically.
facts.quote: When every individual respects another and honours their freedom and rights, dignity of the individual will get established. In such an atmosphere, fraternity will grow automatically.

facts.text: The Preamble ends by mentioning that the people of India have given the Constitution to themselves.
facts.quote: The Preamble ends with a mention of the fact that the people of India have given the Constitution to themselves.

facts.text: The Constituent Assembly made the Constitution of India.
facts.quote: The Constituent Assembly made the Constitution of India.
